title: My Morning Routine
summary: Learn how to talk about your morning. Discover three important daily routine actions.

sections.p: We use the phrase 'wake up' when we stop sleeping in the morning. When your eyes open and you leave your bed, you wake up. This is usually the very first thing we do every single day before we start our busy morning.

ex.en: I wake up at seven o'clock.
You wake up early on Mondays.
ex.mean: You stop sleeping early at the start of the week.

sections.p: After you leave your bed, you need to put on your clothes. We say 'get dressed' for this action. You take off your pajamas and put on a shirt, pants, or a dress for the new day.

ex.en: I get dressed in my bedroom.
ex.mean: I put my clothes on in my room.
She puts on her clothes fast.

sections.p: In the morning, our body needs food and energy. The first meal of the day is breakfast. We use the phrase 'have breakfast' to talk about eating this morning meal.

ex.en: We have breakfast in the kitchen.
ex.mean: We eat our morning food together.

ex.en: Do you have breakfast every day?
ex.mean: Is it your habit to eat in the morning?

tip: Say your morning routine out loud every day. Do the action and speak the English words at the same time!

quiz.en: I open my eyes and stop sleeping. I ___ at seven o'clock.
Now I put on my shirt and pants. I ___.
I eat bread and drink coffee in the morning. I ___.
Breakfast is the first ___ of the day.
